title: B.C. Conservatives drop candidate accused of making comments about Hitler
summary: A B.C. Conservative candidate has been dropped after he was accused of posting offensive remarks on social media.

image.caption: Jordan McIntosh has been dropped as a B.C. Conservative candidate in Vancouver-Strathcona. (B.C. Conservative party website)

blocks.text: British Columbia
A B.C. Conservative candidate has been dropped after he was accused of posting offensive remarks on social media.
Jordan McIntosh dropped as the candidate for Vancouver-Strathcona
The party says Jordan McIntosh is no longer its candidate for Vancouver-Strathcona and that if elected, he will not sit in caucus.

The Conservatives announced his removal from the slate less than an hour after Callista Ryan, the NDP’s candidate for Vancouver-Quilchena, posted screenshots on social media platform X, showing what she said were McIntosh’s posts.
"Looks like Lorne Doerkson's candidate in Strathcona Jordan McIntosh thought he could use a nameless twitter account to say many awful, offensive things," Ryan said.

Looks like Lorne Doerkson's candidate in Strathcona Jordan McIntosh thought he could use a nameless twitter account to say many awful, offensive things, including claims that Hitler didn't "specifically" hate jews and that the holocaust may not have been "the goal". https://t.co/xsxsvuQiob—callistaryan
A post under the account @DeathNight771 made claims that Hitler didn't "specifically" hate Jews and that the Holocaust may not have been "the goal."

McIntosh is a university student working toward a BA in geological engineering, according to his biography, which has since been removed from the party’s website. His LinkedIn page says he attends the University of Waterloo in Ontario.

A party spokesperson speaking on background says McIntosh was informed he was no longer a candidate shortly after Ryan's social media post. McIntosh is 18 years old and the party says it appears the posts were made when he was 15.
The Vancouver-Strathcona riding was previously held by Joan Phillip, who died on Aug. 28.

items: B.C. Conservatives drop Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate after offensive social media posts

blocks.text: Amanda Burrows, who has served as director for First United in the Downtown Eastside, is the NDP’s candidate in that riding. It’s considered one of the safest NDP seats in the province.
This is the second time the B.C. Conservatives have dropped a candidate over offensive social media posts.
Last week, the party fired Joachim Agou in light of social media posts targeting Palestinians and Pakistanis that came to light.
B.C. Conservative Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate dropped after offensive posts
Doerkson has also faced calls from the Unified Muslim Associations of B.C. to drop Katy Merrifield as the party’s campaign director over anti-Islam posts.
Merrifield posted on X in June in response to a U.K. inquiry about child sexual exploitation: "F--k Islam. Defend Western civilization." The post was later removed.

items: B.C. Conservative campaign director under fire for anti-Islam posts

blocks.text: During Wednesday night's B.C. leaders' debate, Doerskon defended Merrifield, saying she made the comments and has since apologized for them. He says he will not remove her.
Doerkson could not be reached for comment on McIntosh’s removal or the party's vetting process.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
